cards.text: This one's a song of ascents, and the singers call themselves "we." They're looking back to when the LORD restored the captives of Zion. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so I'm ALREADY emotional.

cards.question: Here comes the song's first picture. When the LORD restored the captives of Zion, the singers say they were like ___.

cards.text: Mouths full of laughter, tongues full of shouts of joy. This isn't polite smiling, friend, this is LOUD happy, can't-even-hear-the-oven-timer happy.

cards.question: Then other people start talking about the singers. What was said about them among the nations?

answers.text: The LORD has done great things for them
Their own strength has saved them
Their enemies have grown weary of them

cards.question: The nations say, "The LORD has done great things for them." In the very next line, how do the singers change those words?

answers.text: They turn it into a question
They say it about the nations

cards.question: True or false: Right after saying the LORD has done great things for us, the singers say they are filled with fear.
Then the song turns a corner. After all that celebrating over what the LORD has done, the singers ask the LORD to ___ their captives.

cards.text: And they pray it with a picture: "Restore our captives, O LORD, like streams in the Negev." The Negev is the dry land in the south, so picture streams running right through it.
Then the song walks out into a farm field: "Those who sow in tears will reap with shouts of joy." Friend, I've cried into a batch of dough before, and the dough did NOT care.
Then the picture zooms in on one person. He goes out weeping, carrying a trail of seed.

cards.question: True or false: The song says the one who goes out weeping with seed will surely come back.
The one who went out weeping with seed does come back. What is he carrying now?
